Abstract

Multi‐year droughts reduce groundwater recharge, but by how much is uncertain. Using 40 years of well records from California, we show recharge fell by 70% during the 2012–2016 drought and recovered within two wet winters.

Plain Language Summary

Droughts mean less water soaks into the ground. We looked at decades of well data and found that refilling took only two wet winters.

Key Points

  • Recharge fell 70% during drought

1 Introduction

Groundwater supplies a third of irrigation water.

5 Conclusions

Groundwater recharge in California collapses during multi‐year droughts but recovers quickly once wet winters return.

Water managers can plan for short recovery times when setting pumping limits.
